description: Multi-source recall oracle ensemble (GT-building reference, far over budget)
name: 30min

description: Cheap local baseline, first honest measurement since its ~/paddle_env subprocess path broke (fixed to sys.executable; the subprocess is load-bearing, it keeps CUDA uninitialised so vLLM can fork). 0.4051 @ 12.94 sec/page. Over-generates badly on dense issues (1925 211 preds vs 108 GT, 1952 398 vs 197), and paragraph_score 0.1017 -- PaddleOCR region text carries almost no paragraph structure. Still the best LOCAL route, above exp_017 0.4029 at 14x less compute.

NEW RECORD (budget-compliant): Ray-free column-structured 8B route — 3-column split + Qwen3-VL-8B structured-JSON (VLM_OCR_STRUCTURED_V2, 8192 tok) + MergePages + ParseIssue, operators called DIRECTLY in the experiment (no run_pipeline/Ray), VlmOcr loaded once for all 6 issues. 0.4275 avg vs record exp_009 0.4071 (+0.0204) @ 181.98 sec/page (in budget, cap 250). Faithful reproduction of the archived exp_045 config (which was 0.4615 on stale/older GT; on current GT it is 0.4275). ADVERSARIAL REVIEW = real gain, NOT gamed, but FRAGILE/uneven: not overgeneration (preds<GT everywhere, under-generates); holdout does NOT regress (tune 0.3767, holdout 0.3993, gap +0.0226); giant blobs present (1895 worst CER 157) but q-gate+wCER-cap penalize not reward them, so no score inflation. Carried by 1925=0.675 and 1910=0.566; COLLAPSES on dense layouts — 1895=0.128 (22 blobs, median 16.5k chars, 50% >5k chars, 23% high-repetition per probe) and 1935=0.334. 21x the cost of exp_009 (8.66 sec/page) for +0.02. In-budget gain per the any-gain-counts rule; ships only if the per-issue brittleness is acceptable vs exp_009's cheap uniformity.

RECORD. Gemini 3.7-flash, full page in, JSON array out, thinking_budget=128, de-hyphenation, paragraphs recovered from the model's own newlines. HIGH VARIANCE -- five runs gave 0.6258 / 0.6045 / 0.5768 / 0.5583 / 0.6247 (the middle two used a paragraph-structure prompt since reverted); treat ~0.62 as the mean, not a point estimate. paragraph_score 0.3109 vs 0.1819 for a sentence-splitting heuristic on the same output, so its paragraph detection is real. Weak on 1952 (0.423) and over-segments 1935 (419 preds vs 257 GT). sec_per_page is API latency at 12-way concurrency, NOT GPU time; corpus cost ~$5.7k at intro pricing.

REJECTED: exp_018 route with the model swapped to gemini-3.5-flash-lite (one variable). 0.3776 vs 3.7-flash's 0.6115 -- a 38% drop, and BELOW the local exp_017 0.4263. Fails on both axes: UNDER-generates badly (1935 118 preds vs 256 GT, 1952 71 vs 197, 1910 113 vs 196) AND loses text (recall 0.269-0.796 vs 3.7-flash's 0.53-0.98; wCER 0.475-0.796 vs 0.204-0.726). It merges articles and drops content, so the cheaper token rate does not buy a usable route. Not faster either: 15.48 sec/page vs 8.55. Lesson: on dense historical broadsheet the frontier model is doing real work -- the small-model tier is not a cost/quality tradeoff here, it is a different capability class.
